name: Choose the right metric unit
description: Student can identify which metric unit is used to measure a familiar item.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says milk is measured in litres and a person's mass in kilograms.
commonError: Student mixes up units, such as measuring length in grams.
checkpointTask: Name everyday items. Ask the student which metric unit measures each.

name: Use a benchmark to estimate
description: Student can use a known benchmark, such as 1 kg or 1 litre, to estimate a measure.
exampleOfSuccess: Knowing a bottle holds 1 litre, the student estimates a jug holds about 2 litres.
commonError: Student estimates with no reference point.
checkpointTask: Give a benchmark item. Ask the student to estimate a related measure using it.

name: Estimate a length using a known length
description: Student can estimate a length by comparing to a known one.
exampleOfSuccess: Knowing a friend is about 1 metre, the student estimates a tree is about 5 metres.
commonError: Student estimates without using the comparison.
checkpointTask: Pose a length to estimate and give a benchmark. Ask the student to estimate.

name: Choose units to estimate a space
description: Student can choose and use suitable units to estimate the dimensions of a space.
exampleOfSuccess: The student uses metres to estimate the length of the classroom.
commonError: Student chooses a unit that is too small or too large for the task.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to estimate the dimensions of the room and say what units they used.

name: Measure length with a ruler or tape
description: Student can measure the length of an object using a ruler or tape with labelled markings.
exampleOfSuccess: The student measures a book as 24 cm, lining up the zero mark.
commonError: Student starts from the end of the ruler rather than the zero mark.
checkpointTask: Give objects and a ruler. Ask the student to measure each in centimetres.

name: Measure mass with scales
description: Student can measure the mass of an object using kitchen scales.
exampleOfSuccess: The student reads the scale to find a parcel is 300 grams.
commonError: Student misreads the scale markings between numbers.
checkpointTask: Give objects and scales. Ask the student to measure the mass of each.

name: Measure capacity with a jug
description: Student can measure capacity using a measuring jug with labelled markings.
exampleOfSuccess: The student pours water to the 250 mL mark.
commonError: Student reads the jug at eye level incorrectly or ignores the markings.
checkpointTask: Give a jug and containers. Ask the student to measure how much each holds.

name: Read labelled markings accurately
description: Student can read the value at a point between labelled markings on an instrument.
exampleOfSuccess: On a ruler, the student reads a point between 6 and 7 cm as 6 and a half cm.
commonError: Student rounds to the nearest labelled number instead of reading between.
checkpointTask: Point to values between markings on a ruler or scale. Ask the student to read each.

name: Compare measures in the same unit
description: Student can compare two objects by measuring both in the same unit.
exampleOfSuccess: Measuring two ribbons as 18 cm and 25 cm, the student says the second is longer.
commonError: Student compares measurements taken in different units directly.
checkpointTask: Give pairs of objects. Ask the student to measure both and compare.

name: Relate units of time
description: Student can use the relationships between days, hours, minutes and seconds.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says there are 60 seconds in a minute and 60 minutes in an hour.
commonError: Student confuses the relationships, such as 100 seconds in a minute.
checkpointTask: Ask the student how many seconds in a minute, minutes in an hour, hours in a day.

name: Estimate the duration of an event
description: Student can estimate how long an everyday event takes in suitable units.
exampleOfSuccess: The student estimates reading a page takes about 2 minutes.
commonError: Student estimates in units that do not suit the event.
checkpointTask: Name events. Ask the student to estimate how long each takes.

name: Compare durations
description: Student can compare the duration of two events using formal units.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says a 90-second task is longer than a 1-minute task.
commonError: Student compares the numbers without converting to the same unit.
checkpointTask: Give pairs of durations in mixed units. Ask the student which is longer.

name: Check an estimate with a timer
description: Student can use a timer to measure and check an estimate of a short duration.
exampleOfSuccess: The student estimates 30 seconds, times it, and compares.
commonError: Student does not compare the measured time back to their estimate.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to estimate a short duration, then time it and compare.

name: Read an analog clock to the hour and half hour
description: Student can read an analog clock to the hour and half hour.
exampleOfSuccess: The student reads the clock as half past 3.
commonError: Student reads the hour hand as pointing exactly at a number when it is between two.
checkpointTask: Set an analog clock to hours and half hours. Ask the student to read each.

name: Read an analog clock to five minutes
description: Student can read an analog clock to the nearest five minutes.
exampleOfSuccess: The student reads the clock as 25 past 4.
commonError: Student counts the minute marks by ones, or reads the minutes as the small number.
checkpointTask: Set times at five-minute intervals. Ask the student to read each.

name: Read an analog clock to the minute
description: Student can read an analog clock to the nearest minute.
exampleOfSuccess: The student reads the clock as 17 minutes past 9.
commonError: Student rounds to the nearest five minutes instead of reading exactly.
checkpointTask: Set times to the minute. Ask the student to read each.

name: Connect analog and digital time
description: Student can match a time shown on an analog clock to its digital form.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown 'quarter to 8' on an analog clock, the student writes 7:45.
commonError: Student writes the hour as the number the hour hand is nearest rather than has passed.
checkpointTask: Show analog times. Ask the student to write each in digital form.

name: Identify a right angle
description: Student can identify a right angle as a square corner.
exampleOfSuccess: The student points to the corner of a book and says it is a right angle.
commonError: Student calls any corner a right angle regardless of its size.
checkpointTask: Show various corners and angles. Ask the student to point out the right angles.

name: Connect turns to angles
description: Student can connect quarter, half and three-quarter turns to angles.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says a quarter turn makes a right angle.
commonError: Student confuses the size of the turn with the size of the angle.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to make quarter and half turns and describe the angle each makes.

name: Compare an angle to a right angle
description: Student can compare an angle with a right angle and say whether it is bigger, smaller or the same.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown an open angle, the student says it is bigger than a right angle.
commonError: Student compares by the length of the arms rather than the opening.
checkpointTask: Show angles. Ask the student whether each is bigger than, smaller than or equal to a right angle.

name: Find angles in the environment
description: Student can find angles bigger than, smaller than and equal to a right angle around them.
exampleOfSuccess: The student finds a right angle on a window and a smaller angle on a slice of pizza.
commonError: Student finds only right angles, or judges by appearance without comparing.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to find one angle bigger, one smaller and one equal to a right angle in the room.

name: Relate dollars and cents
description: Student can use the relationship that 100 cents make one dollar.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 100 cents is the same as one dollar.
commonError: Student treats cents and dollars as the same size, such as 5 cents equals 5 dollars.
checkpointTask: Ask the student how many cents make a dollar and to convert simple amounts.

name: Make an amount with coins and notes
description: Student can make a given money amount using coins and notes.
exampleOfSuccess: The student makes $2.50 using a $2 coin and a 50 cent coin.
commonError: Student makes the wrong total, or confuses coin values.
checkpointTask: Name money amounts. Ask the student to make each with play money.

name: Represent an amount in different ways
description: Student can represent the same money amount in more than one way.
exampleOfSuccess: The student shows $1 as two 50 cent coins, and as four 20 cent coins and a 20.
commonError: Student gives only one combination, or a combination with the wrong total.
checkpointTask: Give an amount. Ask the student to show it two different ways.

name: Count a mixed collection of money
description: Student can count a mixed collection of coins and notes to find the total.
exampleOfSuccess: The student counts a $5 note, a $2 coin and three 20 cent coins as $7.60.
commonError: Student counts the number of items rather than their value.
checkpointTask: Give a mixed collection of play money. Ask the student to find the total.
